name: P2 · Unit 5 — Database Management Systems
description: 3 of 10 topics so far (6 sets × 30 questions): ER Model & Relational Model; Relational Algebra and Relational Calculus; SQL – Part 1. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

questions.question: The Entity-Relationship (ER) model was proposed in 1976 by:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Codd proposed the relational model (1970).

questions.question: In an ER diagram, a rectangle represents a(n):
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Diamonds are relationships and ellipses are attributes.

questions.question: In an ER diagram, a double line connecting an entity set to a relationship indicates:

options.B: Total participation of that entity set in the relationship

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Every entity in the set must take part in at least one relationship instance.

questions.question: A weak entity set is one that:

options.A: Has more than one primary key
options.C: Does not have a key of its own and is identified through an owner entity

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). It is shown as a double rectangle and linked by a double-diamond identifying relationship.

questions.question: The partial key (discriminator) of a weak entity set is shown in an ER diagram by:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: The owner's key plus the discriminator form the weak entity's key.

questions.question: PAYMENT is a weak entity owned by LOAN (key loan_no); payment_no distinguishes payments of the same loan. The primary key of the PAYMENT relation is:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Primary key of a weak entity = owner's primary key + discriminator.

questions.question: An attribute such as Phone_numbers, which can hold several values for one entity, is called:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: It is drawn as a double ellipse.

questions.question: An attribute such as Age, computed from Date_of_birth, is a:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Derived attributes are drawn with dashed ellipses and usually not stored.

questions.question: An attribute such as Name, made up of First_name, Middle_name and Last_name, is a:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Composite attributes can be divided into smaller parts.

questions.question: A relationship in which an EMPLOYEE supervises another EMPLOYEE is called a:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: The two participations are distinguished by role names (supervisor, supervisee).

questions.question: A relationship set that involves three entity sets is said to have degree:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Degree = number of participating entity sets.

questions.question: In a 1 : N relationship between DEPARTMENT (1) and EMPLOYEE (N), when mapping to relations the foreign key is placed in:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Each employee row stores its department's key.

questions.question: Entity sets A and B are related by a many-to-many relationship R with no attributes of its own. The minimum number of relations needed is:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). One relation each for A and B, and one for R holding both keys.

questions.question: Entity sets A and B have a one-to-many relationship R, and every B entity participates in R. The minimum number of relations needed is:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: R is absorbed into B's relation as a foreign key.

questions.question: A multivalued attribute of an entity is mapped to the relational model as:

options.A: A separate relation containing the attribute and the entity's key
options.D: Extra columns in the same relation

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Elmasri step 6 of the ER-to-relational mapping.

questions.question: Designing lower-level entity sets from a higher-level entity set by identifying distinguishing features (top-down) is called:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Generalization is the reverse (bottom-up) process.

questions.question: Combining several entity sets that share features into a higher-level entity set (bottom-up) is called:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: E.g. CAR and TRUCK generalised into VEHICLE.

questions.question: Aggregation in the ER model is used to:

options.D: Treat a relationship set as an entity so that it can take part in another relationship

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: E.g. a relationship between (EMPLOYEE works-on PROJECT) and MANAGER.

questions.question: In (min, max) notation, (0, N) on an entity's participation in a relationship means:

options.A: Partial participation; an entity may take part many times

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: min = 0 means participation is optional.

questions.question: Hours_worked belongs to the M : N relationship WORKS_ON between EMPLOYEE and PROJECT. When mapped, Hours_worked goes into:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: It describes a pair (employee, project), not either entity alone.

questions.question: Entity sets A and B have a one-to-one relationship with total participation on both sides. The minimum number of relations needed is:
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Both entity sets and the relationship can be merged into a single relation.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A weak entity set always has total participation in its identifying relationship.
II. A weak entity set can be identified without its owner entity.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Weak entities depend on their owner for identification.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Specialization can be disjoint or overlapping.
II. Specialization can be total or partial.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Both constraints apply to specialization/generalization.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A derived attribute must always be stored in the database.
II. A multivalued attribute is mapped into the same relation as extra columns.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Derived attributes are usually computed; multivalued attributes go to a separate relation.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): An M : N relationship needs its own relation when mapped.
Reason (R): A foreign key in either entity's relation could hold only one value per tuple.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: So the pairs must be stored in a separate relation.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Every entity set in an ER diagram must have a key attribute.
Reason (R): Weak entity sets are identified using the key of an owner entity set.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Weak entity sets have no key of their own, so A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Double lines in an ER diagram show total participation.
Reason (R): Peter Chen proposed the ER model.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Both true, but R does not explain A.

questions.question:
Match the ER symbol with its meaning:
a. Double rectangle
b. Double ellipse
c. Dashed ellipse
d. Double diamond

1. Weak entity set
2. Multivalued attribute
3. Derived attribute
4. Identifying relationship
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Standard Elmasri/Chen notation.

questions.question:
Match the concept with an example:
a. Composite attribute
b. Multivalued attribute
c. Recursive relationship
d. Weak entity

1. DEPENDENT of an EMPLOYEE
2. Address (street, city, PIN)
3. EMPLOYEE supervises EMPLOYEE
4. College_degrees of a person
questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: Typical textbook examples.

questions.question: In an EER diagram, a specialization is commonly shown using:

options.B: A circle (or triangle labelled ISA) connecting the superclass to its subclasses

questions.subject: Entity-Relationship Model
questions.explanation: 'd' in the circle means disjoint and 'o' means overlapping.

sets.name: 2 · Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations

questions.question: In the relational model, a relation is formally a:

options.B: Subset of the Cartesian product of a list of tuples
options.C: Sequence of records in a file
options.D: Subset of the Cartesian product of a list of domains

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Each tuple takes one value from each attribute's domain.

questions.question: The relational model of data was proposed in 1970 by:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). In 'A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks'.

questions.question: The number of attributes in a relation is called its:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: The number of tuples is its cardinality.

questions.question: A relation instance has 6 attributes and 40 tuples. Its degree and cardinality are:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Degree counts columns; cardinality counts rows.

questions.question: A domain in the relational model is:

options.A: A set of atomic values an attribute can take

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: E.g. the set of valid 10-digit phone numbers.

questions.question: Which property does a relation have?

options.A: Tuples must be stored in key order
options.D: Tuples are unordered and no two tuples are identical

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: A relation is a set of tuples (in the formal model).

questions.question: A minimal superkey is called a:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: One candidate key is chosen as the primary key; the others are alternate keys.

questions.question: Relation R(A, B, C, D) has A as its only candidate key. How many superkeys does R have?
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Any set containing A is a superkey: 2³ = 8 (choose any subset of B, C, D).

questions.question: Relation R(A, B, C) has two candidate keys, A and B. How many superkeys does R have?
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Sets containing A: 4; containing B: 4; containing both: 2 → 4 + 4 − 2 = 6.

questions.question: The entity integrity constraint states that:

options.B: Every foreign key must be NULL
options.C: A relation must have at least one tuple
options.D: No primary key value can be NULL

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Otherwise the tuple could not be identified.

questions.question: The referential integrity constraint states that a foreign key value must:

options.A: Be larger than the primary key
options.B: Be unique in the referencing relation
options.C: Match a primary-key value in the referenced relation, or be NULL

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). It keeps references between relations consistent.

questions.question: ENROL(roll_no) references STUDENT(roll_no). Which operation can violate referential integrity?

options.A: Deleting a STUDENT tuple whose roll_no appears in ENROL

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Inserting into ENROL with an unknown roll_no is the other way to violate it.

questions.question: Inserting a new tuple into a relation can violate:

options.A: Domain, key, entity integrity and referential integrity constraints

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Elmasri: insertion can violate all four kinds of constraints.

questions.question: A foreign key defined with ON DELETE CASCADE means that when the referenced tuple is deleted:

options.A: The foreign keys are set to NULL
options.D: The referencing tuples are also deleted

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: ON DELETE SET NULL would instead set the foreign keys to NULL.

questions.question: Employee.supervisor_ssn referring to Employee.ssn is an example of a:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: A foreign key may refer to its own relation.

questions.question: In the relational model, NULL can mean:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Its several meanings are why NULLs complicate design.

questions.question: The description of a database (relation schemas and constraints), which changes rarely, is the database:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: The state is the data at a particular moment.

questions.question: Elmasri lists how many informal guidelines (measures of quality) for relation schema design?
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Clear semantics; no update anomalies; few NULLs; no spurious tuples.

questions.question: Storing EMPLOYEE and DEPARTMENT data in one relation EMP_DEPT, so that a new department cannot be added until it has an employee, is an example of:
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Deleting the last employee of a department would be a deletion anomaly.

questions.question: A key constraint (uniqueness constraint) states that:

options.B: No two tuples can have the same value for the key

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Candidate keys uniquely identify tuples.

questions.question: A domain constraint is violated when:

options.C: An attribute value is not from the attribute's domain, e.g. text in a numeric Age field

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Domains define allowed values and types.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A relation can have more than one candidate key.
II. A primary key may contain NULL in one of its attributes.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Entity integrity forbids NULL in any primary-key attribute.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Deleting a tuple from the referencing relation can violate referential integrity.
II. Deleting a tuple from the referenced relation can violate referential integrity.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Removing a referencing tuple leaves no dangling reference.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A foreign key may be NULL unless declared NOT NULL.
II. A foreign key must refer to the primary key (or a candidate key) of the referenced relation.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Both are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Duplicate tuples are not allowed in a relation (in the formal model).
Reason (R): A relation is defined as a set of tuples.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Sets have no duplicate elements.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A superkey is always a candidate key.
Reason (R): A candidate key is a minimal superkey.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: A superkey need not be minimal, so A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Entity integrity prevents NULL primary keys.
Reason (R): Foreign keys can never be NULL.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: A is true; R is false – foreign keys may be NULL.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Insertion anomalies arise in poorly designed relations.
Reason (R): The relational model was proposed by E. F. Codd.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: Both true, but R does not explain A.

questions.question:
Match the term with its meaning:
a. Degree
b. Cardinality
c. Candidate key
d. Foreign key

1. Number of tuples
2. Number of attributes
3. Minimal superkey
4. Refers to a key in another (or the same) relation
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Basic relational terminology.

questions.question:
Match the constraint with what violates it:
a. Domain
b. Key
c. Entity integrity
d. Referential integrity

1. NULL primary key
2. Value outside the allowed set
3. Two tuples with the same key
4. Foreign key pointing to a non-existent tuple
questions.subject: Relational Model, Constraints and Update Operations
questions.explanation: The four basic relational constraints.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental (basic) operation of relational algebra?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Basic operations: select, project, union, set difference, Cartesian product, rename. Joins, intersection and division are derived.

questions.question: The selection operation σ in relational algebra:

options.A: Chooses tuples that satisfy a condition (a horizontal subset)

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Projection π chooses columns.

questions.question: Relation R has 10 tuples, and attribute City has 3 distinct values. How many tuples does π_City(R) return (set semantics)?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Projection removes duplicate tuples.

questions.question: R has 3 attributes and 10 tuples; S has 4 attributes and 5 tuples. R × S has:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Degrees add; cardinalities multiply.

questions.question: For R ∪ S, R − S or R ∩ S to be valid, R and S must be:

options.C: Union compatible (same number of attributes with matching domains)

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Also called type compatible.

questions.question: If R has 10 tuples and S has 6 tuples (union compatible), the number of tuples in R ∪ S lies between:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Minimum when S ⊆ R; maximum when they share no tuples.

questions.question: If R has 10 tuples and S has 6 tuples (union compatible), the maximum number of tuples in R − S is:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: When R and S share no tuples, nothing is removed.

questions.question: Intersection can be expressed using basic operations as:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Hence intersection is not a fundamental operation.

questions.question: A theta join R ⋈_θ S is equivalent to:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Selection applied on the Cartesian product.

questions.question: If R and S have no common attributes, the natural join R ⋈ S is the same as:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: There is no condition to match on.

questions.question: R(A, B) = {(1, a), (2, b), (3, a)} and S(B, C) = {(a, x), (a, y), (c, z)}. How many tuples are in R ⋈ S?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Matches on B = a: (1, a, x), (1, a, y), (3, a, x), (3, a, y).

questions.question: R(A, B) = {(a1, b1), (a1, b2), (a2, b1), (a3, b2)} and S(B) = {b1, b2}. R ÷ S is:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Only a1 is paired with every value of S.

questions.question: The division operator is typically used for queries containing the phrase:

options.D: 'for all' (e.g. students who took all courses)

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Division expresses universal quantification.

questions.question: A left outer join R ⟕ S:

options.D: Keeps every tuple of R, padding S's attributes with NULL where there is no match

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: The right outer join keeps every tuple of S.

questions.question: The rename operator in relational algebra is:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: It renames a relation or its attributes.

questions.question: Which equivalence of selections is valid?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Cascade of selections; selections also commute.

questions.question: Which expression gives the names of employees in department 5 earning more than 50,000?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Select the rows, then project the column.

questions.question: Relational algebra is:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Relational calculus is the non-procedural counterpart.

questions.question: Aggregate functions such as SUM and COUNT are provided in:

options.C: Extended relational algebra (the grouping operator 𝒢)

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: They go beyond the basic algebra.

questions.question: The maximum number of tuples in a natural join of R (m tuples) and S (n tuples) is:
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: When every tuple matches every tuple; the minimum is 0.

questions.question: Which operation is unary?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Selection, projection and rename are unary; the others are binary.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Projection may reduce the number of tuples.
II. Selection may reduce the number of attributes.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Projection removes duplicates; selection keeps all attributes.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Division can be expressed using π, × and −.
II. Natural join can be expressed using ×, σ and π.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Both are derived operations.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Union is defined for any two relations regardless of their attributes.
II. R × S is defined only if R and S are union compatible.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Union needs compatibility; the Cartesian product does not.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Intersection is not a fundamental relational-algebra operation.
Reason (R): It can be expressed as R − (R − S).

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Anything expressible by basic operations is derived.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): σ_City='Mysuru'(R) can return more tuples than R.
Reason (R): Selection returns a subset of the tuples of R.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: A subset cannot be larger, so A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): R ⋈ S equals R × S when R and S share no attributes.
Reason (R): The natural join always removes all tuples with NULLs.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: A is true; R is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Relational algebra is procedural.
Reason (R): Codd introduced relational algebra in 1970.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Both true, but R does not explain A; A holds because an algebra expression states the order of operations.

questions.question:
Match the operator with its meaning:
a. σ
b. π
c. ρ
d. ÷

1. 'For all' queries
2. Choose rows
3. Rename
4. Choose columns
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Common matching question.

questions.question:
Match the operation with its result size (R: m tuples, S: n tuples):
a. R × S
b. R ∪ S (max)
c. R − S (max)
d. R ⋈ S (min)

1. 0
2. m + n
3. m
4. m × n
questions.subject: Relational Algebra
questions.explanation: Bounds on result sizes.

questions.question: A tuple relational calculus (TRC) query has the general form:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: t is a tuple variable and P a formula.

questions.question: A domain relational calculus (DRC) query has the general form:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Variables range over attribute domains.

questions.question: Relational calculus is:

options.C: Declarative (non-procedural): it states what to retrieve, not how

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Relational algebra is procedural.

questions.question: Codd's theorem states that relational algebra and safe relational calculus are:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Any query in one can be written in the other.

questions.question: A query language is called relationally complete if it can express:

options.A: Every query expressible in relational algebra

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: SQL is relationally complete (and more).

questions.question: Which TRC expression is unsafe?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: It describes infinitely many tuples not in EMPLOYEE.

questions.question: A calculus expression is safe if:

options.C: Its result is finite and all values come from the domains of the database

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Safe expressions are the ones equivalent to algebra queries.

questions.question: Which TRC query finds names of employees earning more than 50,000?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Range the variable over EMPLOYEE, then apply the condition.

questions.question: The relational-algebra query π_A(σ_B = 5(R)) in TRC is:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Select with the condition and output only attribute A.

questions.question: The universal quantifier ∀ in relational calculus corresponds to which relational-algebra operation?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: 'For all' queries need ÷ in the algebra.

questions.question: Which identity is used to remove ∀ from a calculus formula?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Universal = not exists a counter-example.

questions.question: In a calculus formula, P ⇒ Q is equivalent to:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Implication rewritten with OR.

questions.question: Query-By-Example (QBE) is based on:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). SQL draws largely on tuple relational calculus.

questions.question: QUEL, the query language of the Ingres DBMS, was based on:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Like SQL, it uses tuple variables.

questions.question: A variable in a calculus formula that is not quantified by ∃ or ∀ is called:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Only the free tuple variable(s) appear in the result.

questions.question: Which of the following CANNOT be expressed in basic relational algebra or safe relational calculus?

options.C: Transitive closure (e.g. all direct and indirect managers)

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KSET / KEA / GTTC papers). Recursive queries need extensions such as recursive SQL or Datalog.

questions.question: An atom of the form t ∈ R (or R(t)) in TRC means:

options.A: Tuple variable t ranges over relation R
options.D: t is a primary key of R

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Other atoms compare attributes with each other or with constants.

questions.question: Which DRC query finds names of employees in department 5 from EMP(Name, Dno)?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Bind d with ∃ and test it; output n.

questions.question: Aggregate functions such as AVG are:

options.A: Not part of pure relational calculus (they are extensions)

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Like basic algebra, pure calculus has no aggregates.

questions.question: A tuple variable in TRC ranges over:
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: In DRC, variables range over domain values.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Tuple relational calculus is non-procedural.
II. Every safe calculus query has an equivalent relational-algebra query.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Codd's theorem.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. {t | ¬R(t)} is a safe expression.
II. Safe expressions always give finite results.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: Complements of a relation are infinite, hence unsafe.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. QBE is based on tuple relational calculus.
II. Relational calculus can express transitive closure.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: QBE is DRC-based; transitive closure is not expressible.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Relational calculus queries describe what data is wanted, not how to get it.
Reason (R): Calculus formulas specify properties of the result rather than a sequence of operations.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: That is what non-procedural means.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Safe relational calculus is more powerful than relational algebra.
Reason (R): Calculus uses quantifiers ∃ and ∀.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: By Codd's theorem they are equally powerful; A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Division in the algebra corresponds to ∀ in the calculus.
Reason (R): QBE is based on tuple relational calculus.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus
questions.explanation: A is true; R is false – QBE is based on DRC.

questions.question:

questions.question:

d. Unsafe expression

questions.question: Which TRC query finds students enrolled in every course (ENROL(sid, cid), COURSE(cid))?
questions.subject: Tuple and Domain Relational Calculus

sets.name: 1 · Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints

questions.question: Which of the following command is used to remove all the records from a table in SQL without removing the table structure?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE empties the table but keeps its definition; DROP removes the table itself. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q19

questions.question:
Match the following.
List-1: (a) DDL  (b) DML  (c) Normal form  (d) View
List-2: i) Virtual table  ii) Organising the data  iii) Set of operations  iv) Defining database

options.A: a – iv, b – iii, c – ii, d – i
options.B: a – iii, b – i, c – iv, d – ii
options.C: a – ii, b – iv, c – i, d – iii
options.D: a – i, b – ii, c – iv, d – iii

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: DDL defines the database, DML is the set of data operations, normal forms organise the data, a view is a virtual table. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q20

questions.question: In a relational database, what does a 'foreign key' do?

options.A: Uniquely identifies a record in a table
options.C: Establishes a relationship between two tables
options.D: Stores large binary data like images or videos

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: A foreign key refers to a key of another (or the same) table, linking the two. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q17

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a relational database?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Cassandra and Firebase are NoSQL stores; Hadoop is a distributed processing framework. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q18

questions.question: In an employee table to include the attributes whose value always have some value which of the following constraints must be used?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: NOT NULL forbids missing values in that column. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: The SQL command used to modify a column inside a table
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: ALTER TABLE … MODIFY / ALTER COLUMN changes a column's definition; UPDATE changes data values. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question:
Identify the valid data types of SQL
I) Character and numeric type
II) Boolean and date-time type
III) Fuzzy and unstructured type
IV) Matrix and vector type
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Standard SQL has character, numeric, Boolean and date-time types. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q89

questions.question: Primary key in DBMS should be
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: A primary key must identify each row (unique) and can never be missing (entity integrity). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q87

questions.question:
Match the following:
List-1: a) MYISAM  b) JOIN  c) FOREIGN KEY  d) AUTO-INCREMENT
List-2: i) References a unique identifier in another table  ii) Automatically increases the value of a field  iii) Storage engine for MySQL  iv) Combines rows from two or more tables

options.A: a – iii, b – iv, c – i, d – ii
options.B: a – ii, b – i, c – iii, d – iv
options.C: a – iii, b – iv, c – ii, d – i
options.D: a – iv, b – ii, c – iii, d – i

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: MyISAM is a MySQL storage engine (InnoDB is the default today). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q74

questions.question: Which group contains only DDL commands?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). DML changes data, DCL controls access, TCL controls transactions.

questions.question: GRANT and REVOKE belong to which category of SQL commands?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). They give and take away privileges.

questions.question: COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVEPOINT belong to:
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: They end or partly undo transactions.

questions.question: Which statement about DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP is correct?

options.A: DELETE always removes the table structure
options.B: TRUNCATE can take a WHERE clause
options.C: DELETE can remove selected rows with WHERE and can be rolled back; TRUNCATE removes all rows; DROP removes the table

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). In most systems TRUNCATE (DDL) commits implicitly, unlike DELETE (DML).

questions.question: CHAR(10) differs from VARCHAR(10) in that CHAR(10):

options.C: Stores up to 10 bytes of binary data only
options.D: Always uses 10 characters of storage, padding shorter values with spaces

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: VARCHAR stores only the actual length (plus a small overhead).

questions.question: A column declared DECIMAL(7, 2) (NUMERIC(7, 2)) can store at most:
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: 7 digits in total, 2 of them after the decimal point.

questions.question: Which statement correctly adds a column Email to the table STUDENT?

options.B: ALTER TABLE STUDENT ADD Email VARCHAR(50);

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Structural changes use ALTER TABLE.

questions.question: The difference between a PRIMARY KEY and a UNIQUE constraint is that:

options.A: A table may have many primary keys
options.B: UNIQUE columns can never contain NULL
options.C: A table has one primary key (no NULLs), but can have several UNIQUE constraints, which usually allow NULLs

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Both enforce uniqueness of the values present.

questions.question: Which constraint ensures that Age entered is between 18 and 60?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: CHECK enforces a condition on each row.

questions.question: A DEFAULT constraint:

options.A: Supplies a value for a column when an INSERT does not give one

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: e.g. Status VARCHAR(10) DEFAULT 'Active'.

questions.question: Which data type is most suitable for storing images or other large binary files?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: BLOB = Binary Large Object; CLOB is for large text.

questions.question: Which command removes the table STUDENT together with its structure?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: DROP removes both data and definition.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. CREATE, ALTER and DROP are DDL commands.
II. INSERT is a DDL command.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: INSERT is DML.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A table can have only one primary key.
II. A primary key can be made of several columns.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: A composite primary key spans several columns.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A FOREIGN KEY must reference a column that is a primary key or has a UNIQUE constraint.
II. A FOREIGN KEY column can never contain NULL.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Foreign keys may be NULL unless declared NOT NULL.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): TRUNCATE is usually faster than DELETE for removing all rows.
Reason (R): TRUNCATE deallocates data pages instead of deleting and logging rows one by one.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: That is why TRUNCATE cannot use a WHERE clause.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): UPDATE is a DDL command.
Reason (R): UPDATE changes the values stored in existing rows.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Changing data is DML; A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A NOT NULL constraint forces every row to have a value in that column.
Reason (R): SQL was originally called SEQUEL at IBM.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Both true, but R does not explain A.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A UNIQUE column can never contain a NULL value.
Reason (R): A UNIQUE constraint prevents duplicate non-NULL values.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Most systems allow NULLs in UNIQUE columns, so A is false.

questions.question:
Match the SQL category with its command:
a. DDL
b. DML
c. DCL
d. TCL

1. CREATE
2. UPDATE
3. COMMIT
4. GRANT
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The four sub-languages of SQL.

questions.question:
Match the constraint with its purpose:
a. PRIMARY KEY
b. FOREIGN KEY
c. CHECK
d. DEFAULT

1. Reference to another table
2. Unique and not null identifier
3. Condition every row must satisfy
4. Value used when none is given
questions.subject: Data Definition, Data Types and Constraints
questions.explanation: Integrity constraints declared in CREATE TABLE.

sets.name: 2 · Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an aggregate function in SQL?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: MAX, MIN, SUM, AVG and COUNT are aggregate functions; the others are clauses. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q33

questions.question: The correct order of SQL expressions is
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Written order: SELECT … FROM … WHERE … GROUP BY … HAVING … ORDER BY. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: In SQL, testing whether a subquery is empty is done using
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: EXISTS (subquery) is true when the subquery returns at least one row. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question:
Which of the following term/terms is/are not SQL join command?
I) Inner join
II) Outer join
III) Exterior join
IV) Interior join
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: SQL has INNER, LEFT/RIGHT/FULL OUTER, CROSS and NATURAL joins; 'exterior' and 'interior' joins do not exist. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q82

questions.question:
Name the SQL built-in functions
I) Count
II) Max
III) Min
IV) Distinct
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: KEA's key accepts all four (strictly, DISTINCT is a keyword used with SELECT and inside aggregates). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q83

questions.question:
Match the following SQL commands to perform undo transactions that have not already been saved to database and in the sequence of commands are executed
List-1: a) Perform DELETE & ROLLBACK  b) Perform ROLLBACK & DELETE  c) Perform ROLLBACK & ROLLBACK  d) Perform DELETE & DELETE
List-2: i) Two time delete operation  ii) Delete first & Rollback  iii) Two time Rollback operation  iv) Rollback first & Delete

options.A: a – i, b – ii, c – iv, d – iii
options.B: a – ii, b – iv, c – iii, d – i
options.C: a – iv, b – iii, c – ii, d – i
options.D: a – iii, b – i, c – ii, d – iv

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Each command pair is matched with the same sequence described in words. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q88

questions.question:
A query returns a "missing keyword" error. What could be the issue?
I. Missing a semicolon
II. Incorrect function syntax
III. Using a reserved keyword
Choose the correct answer from the following options
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: KEA's key gives III only: a reserved word used as a name breaks the parser's expected keyword sequence (Oracle ORA-00905). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q77

questions.question: Savepoint is a part of
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: A savepoint lets a transaction roll back part of its work – a recovery feature. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: Which clause removes duplicate rows from the result of a SELECT?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). SELECT DISTINCT City FROM Customer;

questions.question: The difference between WHERE and HAVING is that:

options.A: WHERE can use aggregate functions directly
options.B: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Aggregates such as COUNT(*) > 5 belong in HAVING.

questions.question: The default sort order of ORDER BY is:
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Add DESC for descending order.

questions.question: Table MARKS has a column Score with values 10, 20, NULL and 30. What does SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(Score) FROM MARKS return?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) ignores NULLs.

questions.question: For the same Score values (10, 20, NULL, 30), AVG(Score) is:
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Aggregates ignore NULLs: (10 + 20 + 30) / 3 = 20.

questions.question: WHERE Name LIKE 'A%' selects names that:
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: % matches any sequence of characters; _ matches exactly one.

questions.question: WHERE Name LIKE '_a%' selects names whose:
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: _ stands for exactly one character.

questions.question: WHERE Salary BETWEEN 20000 AND 30000 is equivalent to:
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: BETWEEN includes both end values.

questions.question: Which condition correctly finds rows where Phone has no value?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Any comparison with NULL using = gives UNKNOWN, not TRUE.

questions.question: What happens when DELETE FROM EMPLOYEE; is executed without a WHERE clause?

options.A: All rows of EMPLOYEE are deleted, but the table remains
options.D: Only the first row is deleted

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Always check the WHERE clause in DELETE and UPDATE.

questions.question: Which statement gives every employee of department 5 a 10% raise?

options.B: UPDATE EMPLOYEE SET Salary = Salary * 1.10 WHERE Dno = 5;

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: UPDATE … SET … WHERE …

questions.question: INSERT INTO STUDENT (Roll, Name) VALUES (7, 'Asha'); leaves the other columns of the new row:

options.C: NULL, or their DEFAULT values if defined

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Unspecified columns take defaults or NULL (and must allow it).

questions.question: Which expression returns the number of different cities in the CUSTOMER table?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: COUNT(DISTINCT column) counts distinct non-NULL values.

questions.question: In logical processing order, which part of a SELECT is evaluated first?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → ORDER BY.

questions.question: A subquery that refers to a column of the outer query and is re-evaluated for each outer row is called a:
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: e.g. employees earning more than their own department's average.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. COUNT(*) counts rows including those with NULLs.
II. SUM ignores NULL values.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Both are standard SQL behaviour.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A column in the SELECT list of a GROUP BY query must be grouped or aggregated.
II. HAVING can be used without any aggregate condition only in Oracle.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: HAVING may use any condition on groups in standard SQL.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. WHERE can contain aggregate functions such as AVG(Salary) > 5000.
II. ORDER BY must come before WHERE.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Aggregate conditions go in HAVING; ORDER BY comes last.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Aggregate conditions are written in HAVING, not WHERE.
Reason (R): WHERE is applied to individual rows before the groups are formed.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Group values do not exist yet when WHERE is evaluated.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): WHERE Phone = NULL returns rows with missing phone numbers.
Reason (R): Comparisons with NULL evaluate to UNKNOWN.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Because of R, the comparison never becomes TRUE; A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows.
Reason (R): ORDER BY sorts rows in ascending order by default.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Queries, Aggregate Functions and Update Statements
questions.explanation: Both true, but R does not explain A.

questions.question:

b. HAVING
